messages:
lina: Customer (acme-corp) opened a case — sustained 502/504s on hosted API during large batching (embedding job ~10k tokens) around 15:12 UTC. They report burst after a token rotation. sample req ids: abc123, abc124.

sam: (ack) can you paste a minimal curl and the edge gateway snippet? which model/route are they hitting?

lina: curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-lite-emb","inputs":["...lots of text..."]}'

edge logs (redacted):
```
[15:12:03] edge.gateway: req=abc123 upstream=auth-proxy-01 status=502 msg="upstream prematurely closed" recv_bytes=0
[15:12:03] envoy: stream 0x7f1 stalled h2.rst_stream: CANCEL
[15:12:04] edge.gateway: req=abc124 upstream=model-host-22 status=504 msg="upstream timeout after 30s"
```

akshay: digging in — we're seeing a pattern: auth-service 95p latency spiked ~400-600ms at same time. edge reported h2 pool exhaustion (blocked on new downstream streams) and a lot of RST_STREAMs. upstreams returned empty body.

maria: repro notes: single request ok. Under concurrency >200 (simulated k6) with the same token rotate timing, 502 ratio goes to ~18% and 504s follow after connection timeouts. Seems like auth key rotation causes short auth-cache misses -> auth calls amplify -> upstream keepalive pool gets saturated.

jaime: quick mitigations for support to offer customer: 1) throttle concurrency from client side (max 50 concurrent streams) 2) temporarily route tenant to a smaller model or dedicated pool 3) flip header X-Force-Direct-Upstream: true to skip midproxy for a short window.

sam: ops/eng-runtime — can you check frontdoor/nginx envoy config: max_concurrent_streams, keepalive pool size, and downstream window settings? Also check connection reuse teardown around key rotation.

akshay: noted: frontdoor currently has h2_max_concurrent_streams=100 and keepalive_pool=120. During spike we observed >300 concurrent attempts which queued and then RSTed. Auth service peaked due to cache invalidation on rotate.

lina: customer said they rotated keys automatically with no gradual rollout. They want a recommended safe rotation procedure and rollback plan.

maria: proposed action plan: 1) short-term: place tenant on dedicated hostgroup + bump keepalive_pool to 300 for 1h, apply client-side concurrency cap; 2) medium-term: add token-rotation canary that staggers cache invalidation, add circuit-breaker on auth calls, add per-tenant upstream reservation; 3) docs: add guidance for rotation (stagger across instances, warm caches).

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421 edge-auth-thrash-502s (P2) — assigned to eng-runtime.

sam: I'll draft a short runbook for CS with the immediate mitigations and the curl snippet they can use to test. Also filing eng-runtime ticket to add backpressure on auth path and per-tenant fallback route.

lina: customer will try the dedicated routing + throttle. I told them to report back within 1h. will post update. :thumbsup:

notes: reproduction steps for engineers included above (k6 script with concurrency ramp to 300 during key rotate). include trace ids abc123/abc124 for correlation.
